nary_nodes.label: Nolan on 'The Odyssey' difficulty
evidence: Filmmaker Christopher Nolan said he knew filming "The Odyssey," which was shot in six countries, "was going to be hard."

"For us, it was just the sheer magnitude of it's 'The Odyssey,' it should be hard. We're going to go out there and we're going to make it as well as we can," Nolan told "CBS Mornings" co-host Gayle King in an interview that aired on Monday.

evidence: "The Odyssey," which Nolan wrote and directed, pulled in more than $260 million worldwide over the weekend.

evidence: It features a star-studded cast, including Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya and Tom Holland.

nary_nodes.label: Damon on 'The Odyssey' difficulty
evidence: "It was the hardest movie definitely that I've ever done," Damon told "CBS Mornings " recently.

nary_nodes.label: 'The Odyssey' first IMAX feature
evidence: The film is also the first commercial feature shot entirely in IMAX.

nary_nodes.label: Nolan's teenage IMAX aspiration
evidence: Nolan said he told himself as a teenager that if he ever had the opportunity to direct a Hollywood film, he wanted "to do the whole thing on IMAX."

nary_nodes.label: Nolan on IMAX benefits
evidence: "It immerses you. The image is so sharp, the color is so clear. It's so much the way your eyes see the world," he said.
"It fills your peripheral vision when it's on the biggest screen possible."

nary_nodes.label: Nolan on IMAX challenges
evidence: But it comes with more challenges.
"The film is huge. … So after each, sort of just under three minutes, you run out of film," Nolan explained.

"So you have to ask the actors on a longer scene to just stay in the emotional state that they're in, however intense that is, and then you quietly reload the camera and keep everybody focused and then start the scene again."

nary_nodes.label: Nolan on film authenticity
evidence: For Nolan, authenticity in the film was key.

nary_nodes.label: Nolan on audience immersion
evidence: "These are great actors. You could stick them in front of a green screen and they'd do amazing," he said.

"But to me, for the audience, if you want to put the audience on the deck of that ship, get out there on a real boat with Matt Damon, with Tom Holland and Zendaya. Put them in the real waves. Get that IMAX camera, put it on that action, and that way you can immerse the audience."

nary_nodes.label: Nolan on getting nervous
evidence: The Oscar winner said he still gets nervous despite his success and years in the entertainment industry.

nary_nodes.label: Nolan on film completion by audience
evidence: "I make films for audiences, for the theater, for the cinema, and so for me, the movie's really not done until the audience kind of tells me what it is. That's what completes the film. It's exciting, but it's scary," he said.

nary_nodes.label: Nolan's childhood inspiration
evidence: Nolan grew up watching filmmakers like George Lucas and Steven Spielberg and for him, "making films on the big screen is very much an attempt to get back to that experience that I had as a kid."
